newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas sales.

text.p: Hong Kong's bullion market ended down from its New York close on overseas sales as professionals bought or sold gold depending on their positions in intra-day trade, gold dealers said on Friday.
Hong Kong gold trade was marked by brisk selling in the morning as Japanese players on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) liquidated long positions, dealers and traders said.
"A higher dollar/yen also sparked gold sales," one trader at an international bank noted.
But the gold price continued to shuttle between the longs and the shorts, boxing itself into a tight range, traders said.

"Basically, when gold was at $382.50-382.80 per ounce, the longs were happy to sell, pushing the market down, and those who were short were happy to buy when gold dropped below $382," said a trader at an international bank's Hong Kong office.

Selling pressure pushed the market down to $381.50 per ounce where it held for a relatively long time with little trade, but later in the day European buyers entered the market looking for bids at around $381.90-382.20 per ounce, sources said.
The market saw resistence at $383 per ounce, but physical players were definitely looking for lower levels, traders said.
"So if the market tests $380 or below $380 per ounce, then I think the physical buyers will come in again," said the chief bullion dealer at a local bank.

Physical demand remained weak, but traders and dealers in Hong Kong and Singapore were optimistic that seasonal factors had pulled up demand and that buying would accelerate in the last months of the year.
Hong Kong bullion ended at US$381.80/382.30 an ounce Friday against New York's US$382.00/50 close on Thursday.
Local gold ended HK$2 higher at HK$3,518 a tael, despite the slight drop in the loco London price, but the difference was not enough to affect premiums, some traders said.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -5 on Friday from a -3 fix on Thursday.
